definition: The local pressure deviation from ambient air pressure, measured in pascals. Its sign changes during a sound wave.
Cycles per second in hertz. A periodic signal at 200 Hz repeats every five milliseconds.
Position within an oscillation, measured as an angle. A delay produces a different phase shift at each frequency.
A component at an integer multiple of a fundamental frequency. Harmonic strengths and resonances shape a voiced sound.
Root mean square. Square each value, average those squares and take a square root to measure the size of an oscillating signal.
A logarithmic ratio. Use 10 log10 for a power ratio and 20 log10 for an amplitude ratio when power scales with amplitude squared. State the reference.
The ratio of desired signal power to noise power over the same interval and bandwidth, often reported in decibels.
A tail of many reflections after a source stops. It can smear a strong vowel over a weaker subsequent consonant.
Electrical output per unit acoustic input under specified conditions, such as millivolts per pascal at 1 kHz.
A microphone's relative response by arrival direction, at a particular frequency. Real patterns change with frequency.
Setting level through the capture chain so quiet detail clears relevant noise without overloading a later stage.
Saturation when an input exceeds a stage's supported range. Reducing volume afterward cannot recover the discarded shape.
Pulse-code modulation. A sequence of quantized amplitudes, with a rate, number representation and channel layout.
Half the sample rate. Signals beyond the representable band can fold into it unless removed before sampling.
Different continuous frequencies producing indistinguishable sample sequences. A later filter cannot identify the original from those samples alone.
Mapping a continuous or high-precision quantity to a finite set of representable values, introducing bounded error under stated conditions.
Controlled noise added before quantization to reduce signal-correlated error, at the cost of a higher noise floor.
Changing the sample grid by filtering and interpolation, while preserving elapsed time and respecting the new bandwidth.
A weighted sum of delayed copies. In a linear time-invariant system it combines the input with the impulse response.
An efficient algorithm for the discrete Fourier transform. It computes projections onto sinusoidal components.
The short-time Fourier transform. Window overlapping frames, transform each, and place their spectra along a time axis.
A weighting applied to a finite frame. Duration and shape trade temporal localization, leakage and frequency resolution.
Overlapping frequency-band weights that pool spectral power into a compact representation. The exact scale and normalization are configuration choices.
An encoder/decoder pair that represents audio for storage or transport. Lossy designs discard selected information.
A language-specific contrastive sound category. Substituting one phoneme for another can distinguish words.
A resonance region of the vocal tract that emphasizes a range of frequencies. Its position helps distinguish vowel qualities.
Timing, pitch movement, prominence and phrasing across speech. It carries structure and interaction cues beyond word identity.
An articulatory gesture changing under the influence of neighboring sounds. A phone's acoustics depend on context.
Alternation among languages or varieties within discourse or an utterance. Evaluation must account for transcription and normalization choices.
A vector of local derivatives of a loss with respect to parameters. A gradient-descent update moves in the opposite direction.
Exponentiate scores and normalize by their sum to produce a distribution across mutually exclusive alternatives.
An expected negative log probability under target labels. For a one-hot target it is the negative log probability of the observed class.
A weighted combination of value vectors, with weights derived from query-key compatibility and optional position masks.
Connectionist temporal classification. It sums probabilities of frame-level paths that collapse into a target sequence after merging repeats and removing blanks.
A sequence model combining acoustic evidence and label history. Its alignment lattice permits time advances and label emissions.
A mapping between acoustic time and labels. A forced aligner conditions on supplied text, which may itself contain errors.
A bounded search that retains multiple promising sequence hypotheses. Wider beams cost computation and can still prune the correct sequence.
A frame-level judgment about whether speech is present. The end of a conversational turn requires a separate decision.
Assigning local speaker labels to time spans in a recording. Overlap may require multiple active labels.
Comparing an utterance with a claimed speaker's enrollment representation using a calibrated acceptance rule.
A system that synthesizes waveform samples from an acoustic representation or parameters. Artifacts may originate upstream of it.
Learning a velocity field along a probability path. A generator integrates that field to transform noise into a conditioned sample.
Selecting a codebook vector, subtracting it, and quantizing the remaining residual with subsequent codebooks.
Variation in packet arrival timing relative to the media clock. A jitter buffer smooths arrivals by spending playout delay.
A bounded-queue signal or policy that slows production when a consumer falls behind. Measure an audio queue in milliseconds as well as bytes.
Estimating a delayed, filtered playback reference and subtracting it from capture while preserving near-end speech.
Deciding when to close an input segment or release a response. A silence threshold and a turn-prediction policy have different evidence.
A short listener response, such as ‘mhm’, that may support the current speaker without requesting the floor.
Simultaneous incoming and outgoing speech streams. Useful interaction additionally requires policies for overlap and interruption.
A generation identifier used to reject obsolete work after interruption or reconnection, even if a callback arrives later.
A document position advanced by confirmed presentation of audio. A device timestamp estimates presentation and cannot prove attention.
A record of where information came from and how it was transformed, including document version and source span.
Selecting potentially relevant stored content for a query. Relevance alone does not establish that a claim is supported.
Records of particular interactions with time and provenance. Updating or deleting them differs from changing a stable user preference.
Word error rate, the minimum substitutions, deletions and insertions divided by reference words under a specified normalization.
Mean opinion score, averaged subjective ratings under a specified listening protocol. Listener population and confidence intervals matter.
Information from the intended evaluation population entering training or selection, making measured generalization optimistic.
Deliberately introducing a timeout, stale event or other controlled failure to observe recovery and invariant violations.
Low-rank adaptation. Freeze a base matrix and learn an update factored into two smaller matrices.
Adaptation that improves new conditions while degrading previously learned behavior. Measure the original domain as well as the target.
Processing seconds divided by audio seconds. It measures an audio production or processing rate separately from startup delay.
Stored attention keys and values for past positions in an autoregressive transformer. It grows with retained context and concurrent sessions.
A value at or below which 95 percent of the observed latency samples fall, using a stated estimation method and failure accounting.
Routing a bounded share of eligible traffic to a new version while monitoring predeclared release and rollback gates.
